_meta.title: Catalogue of the sources cited by the record corpus
_meta.scope: Every work and every observer that a record cites: standard histories, chronicles, veritable records, classical scholarly works and, for the modern period, named astronomers. An entry gives the title in whichever languages the work actually has one, the people responsible for it, a statement of responsibility where that is not a matter of transmission, and the editions consulted. Records cite an entry by key and do not repeat the title; the chapter, leaf or year cited sits with the record, not with the title here. Where the corpus works from a translation or from a quotation in another book, the edition consulted is marked as such, following the Chicago Manual of Style, 18th edition, section 14.260.
_meta.fields: key = source identifier. title = titles by language, with zh-Hans and zh-Hant for works that genuinely have a Chinese title, rom for the romanisation and en for the English title; omitted entirely for an entry that is an observer rather than a work (optional). author = the people responsible, each with name in its own script, rom for the romanisation, role (comp, ed, trans, annot, obs, attr), dates of life or activity, and kind set to group for an institution or collective; omitted entirely where the work is genuinely anonymous (optional). attribution = a statement of responsibility that is not a matter of transmission, such as the institution behind an observation, a corroborating witness or a description of an anonymous author (optional). editions = the editions of the work, each with kind (orig, crit, facsim for a direct citation, trans or quot for an indirect one, cite for a bare reference), consulted set to true on exactly one of them, by for the translator, editor or intermediary, title, year, url, license, and locus_url as a template for citing a single chapter (optional).
_meta.provenance: Compiled and maintained by hand. The first version was aggregated from the bibliographic fields of an earlier form of the corpus, in which every title was already distinct, and every entry since has been edited individually.
caveats: A license is recorded on a consulted edition only where the text is known to be under one. Left empty it means the status was not established, not that the text is free of restriction; anyone reusing an edition should check its own terms.

Fifty-five entries have no editions at all. Each was checked and no freely reachable full text was found, whether because the archive requires an account or because it refuses automated access. An empty editions field is a finding, not a gap.

An edition marked trans or quot means the corpus works from a translation or from a quotation in another book. It does not mean the original is unavailable. Any further edition listed without the consulted mark is the critical edition of the original, where one is known.

No Chinese title is invented for a western work, and no French, Spanish, Italian or Japanese title is supplied for any work, since few pre-modern titles have a settled form in those languages. Only titles the work actually bears are recorded.

Only real authors are recorded as authors. Where a chronicle is genuinely anonymous, as with the Annales Castellani and the Anales Toledanos, the description of its unnamed chronicler is kept as a statement of responsibility instead. Institutions and expeditions such as the U.S. Naval Observatory or the Royal Society are treated the same way.
Modern observation entries, mostly eighteenth to twentieth century astronomers, have an observer but no work, and so carry no title.
The place where al-Battani worked is disputed between al-Raqqa and Antioch, and the records citing him divide evenly. The entry records both rather than choose.
